In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pontine reticular formation provides a direct and powerful excitatory drive to all spinal motoneurons, and that the drive is distributed equally across ipsilateral and contralateral motor columns, across medial and lateral motor column regions, and across flexor and extensors.
the reticulospinals are organized in the same way in neonatal mice as in adult cats and rats.

the pontine reticular formation sends two crossed and two uncrossed pathways to spinal MN pools, which activate MNs at cervical thoracic, and lumbosacral levels, with no apparent selectivity for medial versus lateral motor column MNs, or for flexor versus extensor MN pools.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pontine reticular nucleus provides a single pathway that activates MNs in a similar fashion across all spinal levels, but that there are at least two subpathways, one uncrossing at the level of C1, the other crossing at the level of the pyramids.

the pontine reticular formation contains a population of neurons that project to the spinal cord and that are capable of driving spinal MNs in a pattern that is consistent with a role in the generation of locomotor activity.
the pontine reticular formation is a major source of descending inputs to the spinal cord that can activate MNs throughout the spinal cord and can do so through both crossed and uncrossed pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pontine reticular formation sends a massive, bilateral projection to the spinal MN pools that are responsible for the control of axial and limb musculature.

the pontine reticular formation is a major source of reticulospinally projecting neurons that are organized in a topographic manner, with neurons at the rostral end of the region controlling MNs at the cervical level, and those at the caudal end controlling MNs at lumbar levels.

the pontine reticular formation contains an extensive and diverse population of neurons that can influence the activity of spinal MNs controlling both axial and limb muscles, and that the pontine inputs to spinal MNs are highly organized and functionally segregated.
